content_html:
An organized freezer helps maintain 0°F (−18°C), use food before quality declines, and keep packages from blocking airflow. The key is using zones, readable dates, and freezer-safe containers without packing the appliance so tightly that the door cannot seal properly.

Check temperature and door sealing

An independent thermometer helps confirm compartment temperature. Do not stack packages against the door or leave bags protruding from drawers because even a small seal gap can cause frost and warming.

Group foods into easy-to-recognize categories

Separate meat, vegetables, breads, prepared meals, and small leftovers into drawers or bins. Categories reduce door-open time and keep small foods from disappearing behind large packages.

Label contents and dates

Use freezer-safe containers or bags, remove excess air where appropriate, and label what the package contains and when it was frozen. Keep older items toward the front to reduce freezer burn and waste.

Do not block vents or overpack the appliance

A reasonably full freezer holds temperature well, but air still needs to circulate around manufacturer-designed vents. If drawers will not close or the door needs pressure to latch, reorganize before adding more food.
